title: English Lost Its Web Monopoly But Still Leads Today
hook: The web diversified fast, yet English kept a narrower lead.
closing: Browsing beyond English now opens a large part of the modern web.
question: Which language do you browse in?

segments.say: English fell to 45% of web pages by 2005. The early web was no longer overwhelmingly English.
Arabic online content grew 2,501% over the measured decade. Other languages expanded far faster than English.
English now appears on 55% of websites. It still leads, but no longer monopolizes the web.
